doc.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Working with Woody Herman
summary: Jolly describes a short stint subbing in Woody Herman's band at two Los Angeles clubs, and Herman's generosity with solos.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You went on to play with Richie Kamuka, Buddy Collette, Benny Goodman, Woody Herman, lots and lots of people. What was Woody like for you?

I worked with Woody for about two weeks, maybe four weeks. It was out here, two different clubs, and I believe Nat Pierce couldn’t do it or something so they called me in. And Wally Heider recorded those things. One was “Basin Street West” and the other was “Peacock Lane” I think it was called “Peacock Lane.” No Woody was wonderful. He would just, I know one thing, if there was a piano solo he would let me open it up and if it was only going to be like one chorus, I’d end up playing two or three, which was nice.
Yeah. Then he’d cue the band in wherever he wanted them to come in.
